newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan prepares voters list for elections.
newsitem.headline: Jordan prepares voters list for elections.

text.p: Jordanian Interior Minister Nazir Rasheed announced measures on Sunday to register voters for parliamentary elections scheduled to be held this year.
The official Petra news agency carried a statement by Rasheed saying all new voters or people who had moved since the 1993 election should register before August 1.

Jordan has not officially set the date for the elections, the first to be held since it signed a 1994 peace treaty with Israel, but under the constitution they should be held within four years of the previous poll on November 8, 1993.
The government of Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali, seen as a caretaker government whose main task was to prepare for the elections, has repeatedly said they will be held on time.
Majali's government has angered opposition groups by issuing laws without recourse to parliament in the months leading up to the elections.

The groups protested that an amended press law setting out tough new restrictions on reporting was aimed at gagging criticism of the government and a one-person one-vote law covering the elections themselves would favour pro-government, tribal candidates.
Petra said Majali attended Rasheed's meeting on Sunday with regional governors at which he set out the timetable for updating the list of voters.
"Majali affirmed during the meeting the importance of retaining the democratic image of Jordan, which we hope will be pure and spotless as it was in all the previous elections," Petra said.
